title: Compatible fs charts for a logarithmic cospan
statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and suppose the ordinary scheme fibre product $W=X\times_ZY$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is locally Noetherian. There is a jointly surjective family of affine etale morphisms $H_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a\to W$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with each $A_a$ Noetherian, of the following form. There are affine etale neighbourhoods $Z_a\to Z$, $X_a\to X\times_ZZ_a$, $Y_a\to Y\times_ZZ_a$, and $H_a$ is an affine open subscheme of $X_a\times_{Z_a}Y_a$. With the restricted log structures, there are fs charts $P_a$ on $Z_a$, $Q_a$ on $X_a$, $R_a$ on $Y_a$, and monoid homomorphisms $h_a:P_a\to Q_a$, $k_a:P_a\to R_a$ giving the two actual log morphisms on chart sections and on units. The structural maps induce a homomorphism $Q_a\amalg_{P_a}R_a\to(A_a,\cdot)$; the monoid pushout here is the quotient of $Q_a\oplus R_a$ by the congruence generated by $(h_a(p),0)\sim(0,k_a(p))$. Over every affine open of $W$, finitely many such affine chart neighbourhoods suffice to cover it. In particular the single map $\coprod_aH_a\to W$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. If $f$ is strict [def-per-strict-log-morphism], the family can be chosen with $Q_a=P_a$ and $h_a$ the identity, the chart of $X_a$ being the composite $P_a\to M_{Z_a}\to M_{X_a}$; symmetrically, if $g$ is strict, with $R_a=P_a$ and $k_a$ the identity. No smoothness or Kummer hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69 (etale fs charts); X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164 (compatible cospan charts and pushout Ri). The arbitrary-morphism chart refinement is agent supplied; WANTED Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, section 1, chart lemma.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar w$ of $W$, with images $\bar x,\bar y,\bar z$. Choose a pointed etale fs chart $P\to M_{Z_0}$ at $\bar z$, and refine to an affine $Z_0$. The fs definition supplies the chart covering and the geometric-point lifting lemma supplies the chosen lift of $\bar z$. Base change gives locally Noetherian fs log schemes $X_0=X\times_ZZ_0$ and $Y_0=Y\times_ZZ_0$, with their restricted log structures and the induced pointed lifts. Indeed their underlying projections are etale; an etale morphism is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type, so local Noetherianity follows from the cited ascent lemma. Affine shrinking does not change a chart or its point.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69 (fs charts); scheme inputs: Stacks 01IT, 02GO, 01T6

proof.text: Choose an fs chart $S$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar x$ in $X_0$. Write $A=\mathcal O_{X_0,\bar x}$, $L=M_{X_0,\bar x}$, $F=\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)\subset S$, $T=S_F$, $G=F^{\rm gp}$ and $C=T/G$. Chart localization identifies $L$ with $T\oplus_G A^\times$ and $C$ with $L/A^\times$. Fs face sharpening says that $T$ is fs, $T^\times=G$, $C$ is sharp fs, and $C^{\rm gp}=S^{\rm gp}/G$ is free of finite rank. These statements need only an fs chart, not log regularity.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99 (localization and sharpening)

proof.text: Lift a finite basis of $C^{\rm gp}$ to $S^{\rm gp}$ and extend additively to a group section $s:C^{\rm gp}\to S^{\rm gp}$. For $c\in C$, choose $t\in T$ above $c$. Then $s(c)-t\in G=T^\times$, so $s(c)\in T$. Thus $s|_C$ is a monoid section, and $(c,v)\mapsto s(c)+v$ is an isomorphism $C\oplus G\to T$: its inverse sends $t$ to $(\bar t,t-s(\bar t))$. The final clause of chart localization now gives a chart germ $b:C\to L$ and an isomorphism $C\oplus A^\times\to L$, $(c,u)\mapsto b(c)u$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), p.75, splitting the free characteristic group; explicit basis-lift argument without the group action

proof.text: Express the actual image $a(p)=f^\flat(p)$ of the fixed target chart in these coordinates as $a(p)=b(v(p))u(p)$. Uniqueness of the coordinates makes $v:P\to C$ and $u:P\to A^\times$ monoid homomorphisms. If $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ generate $P$, let $V\subset A^\times$ be the subgroup generated by $u(p_i)$. Put $Q=C\oplus V$ and $h(p)=(v(p),u(p))$. This is an fs monoid: it is generated by generators of $C$ and $u(p_i)^{\pm1}$; it embeds in $C^{\rm gp}\oplus V$; and $n(c,v)\in C\oplus V$ implies $c\in C$ by saturation of $C$. The map $q:C\oplus V\to L$, $(c,v)\mapsto b(c)v$, has inverse image of $A^\times$ exactly $\{0\}\oplus V$. Its associated-log pushout is $C\oplus A^\times$, since $[(c,v),u]\mapsto(c,vu)$ and $(c,u)\mapsto[(c,1),u]$ are inverse. Consequently $q$ is a chart germ and $qh=a$ exactly, including unit factors. This is a quotient computation from the chart definition.

source.place: Agent expansion of VI 1.1 and 3.7(a): adjoining the finite subgroup of unit coordinates of the fixed target generators

proof.text: Apply fine-log stalk chart spreading to the fs monoid $Q$ and the specified chart germ $q$, obtaining an affine pointed etale $X_1\to X_0$ with chart $Q$. On $X_1$ compare the two homomorphisms $P\to M_{X_1}(X_1)$, namely its $Q$ chart composed with $h$ and the actual pullback of the $P$ chart via $f^\flat$. Their germs agree by $qh=a$. Since $P$ is finitely generated, finite-monoid stalk-data spreading gives one further affine pointed etale refinement $X_a\to X_1$ on which the homomorphisms agree. Restricting preserves the chart. The associated-log universal property shows that the resulting log map is the actual morphism: both agree on every chart element and send a local unit to its pullback. In local associated-log notation both maps are $[p,u]\mapsto[h(p),f^\sharp(u)]$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), p.75, spreading a prescribed splitting; VI 1.1, p.69, associated-log convention (arbitrary-morphism equality supplied explicitly by agent)

proof.text: Perform steps 2--5 for $Y_0\to Z_0$ at the induced point $\bar y$, keeping the same $P$ chart on $Z_0$ throughout: use its own initial fs chart, its own sharp characteristic and its own finite subgroup of unit coordinates. This gives affine pointed etale $Y_a\to Y_0$, an fs chart $R$, and $k:P\to R$ representing $g^\flat$ and its unit pullbacks. Composites of the etale refinements in steps 1--6 are etale. If $f$ is strict, replace steps 2--5 on its side by the pulled-back $P$ chart: by the definition of strictness the log structure on $X_0$ is the one associated to that prelog chart. On any affine pointed open neighbourhood take $Q=P$ and $h=\mathrm{id}$. The other side's construction is unchanged. If $g$ is strict use the same prescription on its side; it also works when both are strict.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.3.4(ii), pp.107--108 (strict pullback); repeat the explicit preceding construction for the second leg

proof.text: Form $B_a=X_a\times_{Z_0}Y_a$. It is affine by the affine fibre-product lemma. Its map to $W$ is etale: first $W\times_ZZ_0\to W$ is a base change of $Z_0\to Z$; next replacing $X_0$ by $X_a$, and then $Y_0$ by $Y_a$, gives two more base changes of etale maps. The composite is $B_a\to W$. The two chosen pointed morphisms from $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ to $X_a,Y_a$ have the same pointed map to $Z_0$, so the fibre-product property gives a point of $B_a$ over $\bar w$. As $W$ is locally Noetherian, so is $B_a$ by etale local finite type and Noetherian ascent. Choose an affine open $H_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ about that point with $A_a$ Noetherian, using the defining locally Noetherian cover. An open immersion is etale, so $H_a\to W$ is etale. Take these neighbourhoods for every geometric point of $W$, and include their affine Noetherian open refinements; they are jointly surjective.

source.place: X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164 (common chart products); Stacks 01I4, 01JQ, 02GO, 01T6, 01OV

proof.text: On $H_a$, let $\beta_Q:Q\to A_a$ and $\beta_R:R\to A_a$ be the two chart structural maps. Compatibility with the actual log morphisms gives $\beta_Q(h(p))=\beta_R(k(p))$ for every $p\in P$: both are the pullback of the structural image of $p$ on $Z_0$. Therefore $(q,r)\mapsto\beta_Q(q)\beta_R(r)$ takes equal values on $(h(p),0)$ and $(0,k(p))$. It descends through the stated generated congruence, yielding the required homomorphism $Q\amalg_PR\to(A_a,\cdot)$. Multiplication and the identity descend because the relation is a monoid congruence.

source.place: X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164, formula $R_i=P_i^{\prime}\oplus_{P_i}Q_i$; explicit monoid quotient verification

proof.text: Let $D\subset W$ be affine. The open preimage of $D$ in each $H_a$ is locally Noetherian, hence has an affine open cover with Noetherian coordinate rings, by the definition and its open-restriction clause. These opens are among the allowed affine refinements and remain affine opens of the corresponding $B_a$. Their images in $D$ are open by etale openness, and jointly cover $D$. Since an affine scheme is quasi-compact, finitely many of these images cover $D$, with each chosen map landing inside $D$. This proves precisely the asserted finite chart-cover property. Each $H_a\to W$ is flat by the definition of etale, so these same finite affine opens verify the fpqc family definition.

source.place: Stacks topologies.tex, lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT, lemma-etale-open; properties.tex Tag 01OV; agent explicit finite-image argument

proof.text: The scheme coproduct $H=\coprod_aH_a$ exists with the $H_a$ as disjoint open components. The map $H\to W$ is flat: at a point of $H_a$, its map on local rings is exactly the flat map for $H_a\to W$. For an affine $D\subset W$, the finitely many affine opens from step 9 are also affine opens of $H$, and their images have union $D$. The singleton $\{H\to W\}$ is therefore an fpqc covering by the same definition, even if the index set is infinite. If $W$ is empty take the empty family and its empty coproduct; the finite-cover condition is then witnessed by zero opens.

source.place: Stacks schemes.tex, disjoint-union construction; topologies.tex Tag 022B, definition-fpqc-covering; elementary componentwise verification
